newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Germany's WAZ buys 70 pct of Bulgarian Pressgroup.
newsitem.headline: Germany's WAZ buys 70 pct of Bulgarian Pressgroup.

text.p: Germany's WAZ Group, publisher of the Westdeutsche Algemeine Zeitung, said on Friday it had bought a 70 percent stake in Bulgaria's 168 Hours Pressgroup.
Erich Schumann, chairman of WAZ directors' board, said the group's deal was a long-term committment.
"At the moment the Pressgroup is in good financial health and we will implement an expansive policy in the future and if necessary finances will be invested," Schumann told a news conference.

Last month the WAZ settled a 23.5 million mark debt of the Pressgroup owed to First Private Bank (FPB), one of five banks slated for bankruptcy by the central bank as part of a reform package agreed with international lending institutions.
The Pressgroup, established in 1990, initially had debts of 29 million marks to FPB but they were reduced by 19 percent after negotiations with the German buyers, bank officials said.
An ambitious printing house project launched last year produced financial difficulties for the Pressgroup, whose weekly papers have a combined circulation of over two million.

"As soon as equipment is installed in the printing house we will use its most modern technology...and will achieve western quality in editing newspapers and magazines," he said through an interpreter.
Schumann said his group, which also has publications in Austria and Hungary, had studied offers from Latvia and Ukraine but they had not suited the German giant.
"We are foreigners and will rely on our prosperous partners (the Pressgroup) as regards editorial policy ," he said.
He praised the editorial and publishing policy of the 24 Hours daily, one of Bulgaria's most popular dailies that is run by the 168 Hours Pressgroup.
Schumann declined to give details of the Pressgroup's new policy on the Bulgarian market or of WAZ's planned investments.
"We wish to give a signal that Bulgaria is opening up to Europe," Schumann said.
